bullets.title: Anthropic IPO Filed: $16.3B H1 Revenue, $657B+ Compute Commitments, Nasdaq Ticker ANT
bullets.body: Anthropic filed for IPO on Nasdaq (ANT) with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as joint lead bookrunners; timing TBD but IPO expected week of Nov 9. H1'26 revenue reached $16.3B (~14x YoY), adjusted operating margin swung to +19% in Q2 from -129% a year prior, and the customer base with $100K+ TTM spend grew from 950 to 11,900 YoY. Compute commitments total $657B+ across Microsoft ($44.9B+), Google ($114.5B+), Amazon ($110B), Broadcom ($161.2B), and SpaceX.AI ($120.5B), with 50.1% founder voting control post-IPO.

bullets.title: AWS Capacity Sold Out Through 2027-2028; AI Capex Cycle Extends Well Beyond Near Term
bullets.body: Amazon CEO confirmed compute is sold out for 2026 and largely committed for 2027, with a meaningful portion of 2028 already booked on $220B capex. Morgan Stanley forecasts hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT) will increase capex >50% in 2027 vs 2026, and raises net US power shortfall estimate to 38GW through 2028 (from 33GW prior). Inference costs still need to fall ~90% for pervasive enterprise adoption per AMZN CEO; AI infrastructure bottlenecks won't alleviate in 2027.

bullets.title: META Raises $95B ($35B Offering + $60B ATM) for AI Capex; NVDA, AMD, AVGO Buy $5B Aggregate
bullets.body: META launched a $35B common stock offering plus a $60B ATM program (not commencing until Q1 2027 when Class C shares begin trading) to fund AI infrastructure. AMD, AVGO, and NVDA each subscribed ~$5B in the Class A raise in what analysts describe as circular financing — META returns capital used to purchase their chips. META targets $211B in CY27 capex vs ~$140B in CY26; the raise is seen as clearing equity overhang heading into 2027.

bullets.title: Neocloud Financing Stress Intensifying; Musk Warns Debt Markets Shutting for AI-Only Revenues
bullets.body: Elon Musk stated that debt markets are nearly closed to AI data center companies without broader revenue streams, flagging potential consolidation among 200+ neoclouds. SpaceX closed a $40B GPU borrowing backed by its diversified business rather than AI revenue, illustrating the divergence. CRWV, NBIS, and IREN are down 57-79% from 52-week highs; S&P Global separately warns data center projects face growing downgrade risk amid local pushback.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Valuations Now Attractive; UBS Says Stocks Discounting 25-30% Cuts to 2028 Compute Forecasts
bullets.body: UBS argues semiconductor valuations have become very attractive as stocks are pricing in approximately 25-30% cuts to 2028 compute capacity forecasts. Key debates remain unresolved before investors gain full conviction for a move higher. GPU rental prices are rising (B300 +10.6% MoM, B200 +13.0% MoM, MI300X +5.3% MoM), and Nvidia's Jensen Huang says a memory glut by 2029 is unlikely given LPDDR and AI demand absorption.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Bearish Nasdaq Trend; Shorts QQQ Bounces, Adds Nvidia to Short List
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough maintains a bearish TREND on QQQ and added Nvidia to his short list after Friday's confirmation of trend breakdown; he prefers shorting QQQ over XLK as MSFT and AAPL retain bullish signals. High-yield OAS sits at ~337 bps with shorts maintained; 10-year yields holding at ~5.10% resistance after Treasury shorts were covered. S&P 500 first significant lower-high is flagged at ~7,600; consumer staples (XLP) rotated to bullish while healthcare is described as the strongest sector long.

bullets.title: Macro Regime: 10Y at 4.99-5.10%; Core Inflation Running Above Fed's ~30bp/Mo Target
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.99-5.10%, with Hedgeye citing four upside inflation pressures: war impact, AI electronics pricing, end of tariff refunds, and annual price resets. If unemployment holds at 4.2% or below, the Fed has little room to tolerate overshoot and financial tightening risk increases. The Dallas Fed ISM-equivalent fell to 53.3 from 58.3 in October, and October ISM Manufacturing PMI tracked at 52.4 vs 54.5 in September, reflecting moderating growth with rising input/output prices.

bullets.title: Midterms: Democrats Strongly Favored for House; 55% Edge on Senate Per Piper Sandler/22V
bullets.body: Polling strongly suggests a big Democratic night with Republicans unlikely to retain the House majority; Democrats hold a 55% edge to take the Senate with ten races within three percentage points. Historical polling error in Senate races runs 2-5 points from final averages. Post-midterm seasonality has historically been favorable: S&P 500 up every year after midterm elections since 1950, with average 15-17% gains.

bullets.title: Israeli Election Outcome Could Reduce Oil Risk Premia; Diplomatic Solution in 1H 2027 More Likely if Netanyahu Loses
bullets.body: A Netanyahu defeat would reduce the probability of renewed US-Israeli military strikes on Iran and likely cause elevated oil market risk premia to recede. GCC leaders would be more likely to push for a successful US-Iran diplomatic outcome, with an eventual solution in 1H 2027 becoming more probable. Coalition formation uncertainty remains, and caretaker period dynamics limit dramatic escalatory actions.

bullets.title: Brazil: Presidential Election News Drives ~20% Selloff in EWZ; CAD Narrows to 2.3% of GDP
bullets.body: Brazilian equities (ABEV, ITUB, ARCO) fell sharply and EWZ dropped ~20% on Presidential election news. Separately, Brazil's current account deficit narrowed to 2.3% of GDP in September (vs expected US$6.3B; actual US$5.1B) — the tightest since 2024 — but portfolio outflows of $2.1B in equities/debt are expected to continue in October given market dynamics. JPM projects the CAD to end 2026 at 2.3% of GDP.

bullets.title: AI Cloud Demand: AWS and SpaceX Both Confirm Supply Constraints; Spot Compute Prices Rising Third Consecutive Week
bullets.body: SpaceX reports cloud demand outstripping supply and monetizing at favorable pricing as the market tightens; AWS capacity for 2026 is sold out, 2027 largely sold out, and a good portion of 2028 already committed. Compute spot prices rose for the third consecutive week (H100 +5.7% to $2.99/hr, B300 +1.6% to $7.64/hr). ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent placed over $35B in Nvidia chip orders; Nscale is in talks with Anthropic on a $45B AI cloud deal.

bullets.title: Data Center Backlash Creating Measurable Political Shift; Could Flip Key House Races
bullets.body: Democratic support among voters within 2 km of data centers rose 7 percentage points (54% to 61%) between May-October 2026, versus only +2 points for voters farther away. Among Trump 2024 voters near data centers, 17% now intend to vote Democratic vs. 6% of those farther away, a divergence that emerged over summer 2026. The backlash could influence House races in Nevada's 2nd, Colorado's 4th, and Ohio's 15th districts; half of Americans oppose data center construction within 3 miles of homes per PF Global/Politico.

bullets.title: VIX Jumps 8.2% to 17.86; Broad Tape +0.9% to 7,691 as Markets Digest Heavy AI/Capex Newsflow
bullets.body: VIX jumped 8.2% to 17.86 while the S&P 500 gained 0.9% to 7,691.36, with S&P futures pre-market at +0.3%. Large-cap growth stocks were down 0.5% last week for the second consecutive week; Semis fell -2.1% and Media fell -6.4%. High Yield saw outflows for the third consecutive week, and Goldman's VIP basket is in its worst 75-day stretch vs the S&P this century outside the GFC.

bullets.title: Hedge Fund De-Risking: Net Leverage at Extreme Lows After Violent AI/Tech Selloff
bullets.body: Market is experiencing what Jefferies describes as traumatic hedge fund de-risking with net leverage at extreme lows following the AI and tech selloff. Retail equity volumes are down 20% since summer and 45% from recent peaks, weakening dip-buying firepower. QQQ took in money while small cap suffered chunky withdrawals; tech saw big inflows concentrated in semiconductors; High Yield saw outflows for three consecutive weeks.

bullets.title: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Exploration Underway; Salesforce Acquires Braze for $5.66B in Active M&A Week
bullets.body: Elon Musk announced Tesla and SpaceX formed a special committee to explore a merger before the end of Trump's term. Key M&A this week: Salesforce acquiring Braze for $47.50/share (~$5.66B EV); Datadog submitted a ~$4B bid for Upwind Security; Instacart is exploring a sale at a potential $16-17B valuation (~$65/share, 10x 2027E EBITDA). Visa was in advanced talks to acquire Fireblocks for ~$2.5B (Fireblocks denied).

bullets.title: MSFT Offers Buyouts to 60,000 Employees as Cost-Cutting Measure
bullets.body: Microsoft launched a voluntary buyout program targeting 60,000 workers across several business divisions as part of a broader cost-cutting effort. This follows broader tech sector workforce rationalization trends including eBay cutting ~1,000 jobs (9% of workforce) in 2026.

bullets.title: Streaming Fragmentation Accelerates: Netflix + Disney Hit Record-Low 25% Combined Share; UGC Exceeds 30%
bullets.body: Streaming reached 50% of all US TV viewing hours for the first time in August 2026 per Citi/Nielsen data, but Netflix and Disney combined fell to a record-low 25% of streaming hours. Paid professionally produced content dipped below 50% of streaming hours for the first time, with user-generated content now exceeding 30% of streaming viewing and free professionally produced content at 20%.

bullets.title: Power Shortfall Estimate Raised to 38GW Through 2028; BTM and Infrastructure Plays in Focus
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd raised the 2026-2028 net power shortfall to 38GW from 33GW, driven by 116GW of chip-driven power demand, increasing urgency for behind-the-meter solutions (BE, SEI) and powered shell providers (WULF, HUT). MS projects US data center demand spillover into APAC. Starlink is separately in talks to access 80,000 US cell sites, raising competitive pressure on telco incumbents globally.

bullets.title: Post-Midterm Seasonality Historically Favorable; FOMC Meeting Wednesday with 10Y Near 5%
bullets.body: S&P 500 has risen every year following midterm elections since 1950, with average gains of 15-17%; this week's clearing events (Anthropic S-1, META raise, mega-cap earnings, ORCL Investor Day, FOMC) may resolve near-term uncertainty. FOMC meets Wednesday with the 10-year yield at 4.99% and curve flattening; one strategist notes that 10-year below 5% with oil at $80 is constructive but 10-year below 5% with oil at $100 is not.

bullets.title: Apple iPhone Duo: 3-Month+ Wait Times at Pre-Launch Signal Strong Demand
bullets.body: UBS Evidence Lab tracking shows iPhone Duo wait times exceed three months as of one day pre-launch, tracked across 30+ countries as a demand proxy. Historical wait-time data has been tracked since 2017 across the top 25 Apple phones in the US.
